title: DC-area forecast: Bright and beautiful through Labor Day; warming midweek
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Mostly sunny and less humid today. After starting in the 60s this morning, we'll reach afternoon highs in the glorious upper 70s to low 80s.

What’s next? Labor Day is a lot like today. Trending warmer Tuesday and Wednesday but still not too humid. A chance for showers and storms could return Thursday as a front approaches.

Today’s daily digit — 9/10: Not a gripe in sight with plenty of sun and a less humid feel. Enjoy!| 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

Forecast in detail

Today (Sunday): Plenty of sunshine with afternoon highs in the upper 70s to low 80s. Light winds from the northeast lock in the less humid feel (dew points near 60). Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tonight: It's a great evening to enjoy the extended weekend outdoors — perhaps at a fire pit — as readings fall through the 70s. Overnight lows in the upper 50s to low 60s are a touch cooler than average. Confidence: High

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow (Labor Day): High pressure settles in overhead, bringing plenty of sunshine and continued comfortable humidity. Highs are in the pleasant upper 70s to low 80s again. Enjoy! Confidence: High 😎 Nice Day!

Tomorrow night: Another great evening to be out and about, with partly cloudy skies and temperatures dropping back through the 70s. Overnight lows in the low to mid-60s. Confidence: High

A look ahead

Mostly sunny and a bit warmer Tuesday with highs back in the mid- to upper 80s, but humidity stays on the low side. Partly cloudy Tuesday night with lows in the 60s. Confidence: High

Feeling more like summer Wednesday and Thursday with highs in the upper 80s to near 90 under partly to mostly sunny skies. Humidity is up a bit by Thursday, when an approaching frontal boundary could bring a chance of showers and storms. Confidence: Medium

DC weather history for September 6

Tropical systems shaped this date, with Hurricane Fran’s remnants in 1996 bringing flooding and damage, and Tropical Storm Hanna in 2008 setting a rainfall record and soaking the region.
